notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already spent when this part began (the first two searches were refused), so nothing here comes from a search engine. Every page was opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, one request a second per site and each site's robots.txt obeyed: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (learned by running the kit's own step, python -m ballot.local_sites files, on a scratch copy of the database; the real database was only read), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list and local party units' sites, the Legislative Reference Library, and local newspapers through their own search pages.

Not read, and nothing worked around: charlesformn.com, swtransit.org and chisagogop.org (each answered the script with a bot check); popecountymn.gov (it refused the script's request for robots.txt with a 403, which is read as stay out, so Stephanie Rust has no official page here); votemoga.com (its robots.txt asks all scripts to stay out, so it is not confirmed as anyone's campaign site); pineknotnews.com and the search pages of pctribune.com (robots.txt); ottertaildfl.com (HTTP 429); nicholashanson.com (HTTP 403; not confirmed as anyone's campaign site). The Minnesota Judicial Branch's site and the state's mn.gov pages were not requested at all, since other parts found they refuse scripts; so neither judge has an official page here.

John DeGeorge: the campaign website he filed with the Secretary of State (degeorge4sheriff.com) had no address on the network on October 1, 2026 (address lookups repeated over several minutes found no such host), so no website is recorded for him.
Nicholas Hanson: the Minnesota DFL's list links only a social media page under his name, which is not a campaign website, so none is recorded.

Republican endorsement of Jason Rarick: no party page that publishes one for 2026 was found. The Pine County Republicans list him as the sitting senator and link his site (their page of 2026 endorsed candidates is statewide offices only); the Carlton County Republicans list him among elected officials; the Kanabec County Republicans' home page names no legislative endorsement; the Chisago County Republicans' site showed a bot check.

Party pages read for the candidates for nonpartisan offices, none of which names anyone in this part: the candidates pages of the Senate District 33, 45 and 49 DFL units, the Senate District 36 DFL's home and elected-officials pages, the Senate District 48 DFL's home page, the Carver County Republicans' 2026 elections page, and the home pages of the Senate District 31 and 32 Republicans.

Read and left out on purpose: work. For four candidates (Patrick Moga, Ardie Anderson, Tony Arndt and Henry C. Ambelang) the pages read describe jobs, some of them with a county, a city or the courts; a job is not a public office held, so none is recorded and none is described here. The pages are the Winona Post's county board story of September 23, 2026, ABC Newspapers' East Bethel voters guide of October 5, 2024, the candidate's own site, and KAXE's filings story of May 20, 2026. An age printed without a year (ABC Newspapers, for Ardie Anderson) was not turned into a birth year.

Sitting legislators (Jason Rarick, Amanda Hemmingsen-Jaeger, Cheryl Youakim, Jay Xiong): only a website, an endorsement, own words and review items are recorded, plus a birth year for the two whose roster record has none (Hemmingsen-Jaeger, Xiong). The Library's other entries for them (earlier city and advisory posts) are left to the roster.

For the second reader: (1) Jason Rarick's site is his committee's own ("Prepared and Paid for by Rarick for Senate") and names the office, but it names no year and its pages read as written for an earlier Senate run. (2) Jay Xiong's birth year: the Legislative Reference Library prints "12/??/1983 (uncertain)"; Wikipedia's article says "born 1983" and cites a Pioneer Press election profile of October 23, 2018, which was not read. (3) Greg Urban: the tie between the 2026 candidate for mayor and the council member in the 2022 story is the name and the city; two letters to the editor in the same paper in September 2026 (opinion, not cited) speak of Greg Urban, running for mayor, as a former council member. (4) Theresa Marie Cermak: the city's tenure list is a PDF, read with the kit's own PDF reader; it shows her on the council in its rows for 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 and counts "Theresa Marie Cermak 4" years. (5) Michael L. Kearney's and Ardie Anderson's start years rest on the government page's term dates together with a newspaper's report of the swearing-in or the election. (6) Tanya Olympia O'Brien: the Pioneer Press reported her appointment in 2018; that she sits today rests on a Sun Thisweek court story of June 5, 2026 that titles her Judge. (7) Jill Christenson's own words are about her 2022 election, as the quote itself says. (8) McKayla Hatfield's chair of SouthWest Transit is in her own site's words; the transit agency's site could not be read.

Seen on official pages about these races, for whoever keeps the record: the seat is open in Carlton County District 2 (the county's page lists Marv Bodie there today), in the Traverse County sheriff's race (the county's page names Trevor J. Wright as Sheriff) and in Owatonna's Fifth Ward (the city's page lists Brent Svenby). KAXE (August 13, 2026) reports that Cass County District 4 held a primary on August 11, 2026, and that Tyler Seifert and the sitting commissioner, Scott D. Bruns, advanced; our record carries the November list only. Glencoe-Silver Lake's own page introducing its school board candidates says of Timothy Dilworth that no response was received by its deadline.

Nothing citable was found for ten candidates, who are listed with no findings: Ann Gustafson, Patrick Moga, Tyler Seifert, Stephanie Rust, Andy Miller, Thomas Wavra, Dale A Fairbanks, Mark Lelwica, Timothy Dilworth and Henry C. Ambelang. None of them filed a campaign website, none sits today on the body they are running for (by that body's own page, where it could be read), and a few likely addresses that were tried turned out to be unrelated or parked sites.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every url in the file was opened again with the kit's honest User-Agent. 42 findings checked, 40 kept, 2 removed (listed under "removed"), 8 reworded so that each says only what its own cited page says: references to newspaper stories with no url in the file were cut from Kearney, Anderson, Bayliss, Borchers and O'Brien; Anderson's start year (the page gives only the term's end) and O'Brien's "now" (the 2018 story cannot show it) became "not stated"; Urban's end is 2022 alone; Rarick's website note keeps only what the site and the Secretary of State's file show, and his review item says only what the roster table holds. The earlier notes are the researcher's and were not re-checked beyond the urls in the findings. District anchors were checked against sl_races; the filed addresses were confirmed by counting matches in John's saved Secretary of State files, with no other column read.
